title: The Frog Prince
author: The Brothers Grimm (retold)
summary: 泉に金のまりを落とした王女。拾ってくれたカエルと、しぶしぶ約束をしますが……。グリム童話「かえるの王さま」を易しく。

source.note: Retold in simpler English from the Brothers Grimm’s “The Frog King, or Iron Henry” (1812, public domain).

paragraphs: Long ago, there was a king who had several beautiful daughters. The youngest daughter was the most beautiful of all. Near the castle there was a big dark forest, and in the forest, under an old tree, there was a deep well.

On hot days, the youngest princess liked to sit by the cool water of the well. She always brought her favorite toy, a golden ball. She threw it up into the air and caught it again. She played this game for hours.

One day, she threw the ball too high. She tried to catch it, but it hit the ground, rolled away and fell into the well. The well was so deep that she could not see the bottom. The princess began to cry, and she cried louder and louder.
Then she heard a voice. “What is wrong, Princess? You are crying so much that even a stone would feel sorry for you.”
She looked around. She saw a frog. It had put its fat, ugly head out of the water.
“Oh, it’s you, old water-splasher,” she said. “I am crying because my golden ball has fallen into the well.”
“Don’t cry,” said the frog. “I can help you. But what will you give me if I bring your ball back?”
“Anything you want, dear frog,” she said. “My dresses, my pearls, even the golden crown on my head.”

“I don’t want your dresses or your pearls or your crown,” said the frog. “But if you will love me and let me be your friend, if I can sit next to you at the table, eat from your little golden plate, drink from your cup and sleep in your bed, then I will bring your ball back.”
“Yes, yes, I promise,” said the princess. But she thought, “What a silly frog! He lives in the water with the other frogs. He can’t be a friend to a person.”
The frog went down into the water. After a short time, he came up again with the ball in his mouth and threw it on the grass. The princess was very happy. She picked up her ball and ran away.
“Wait! Wait!” called the frog. “Take me with you! I can’t run as fast as you!” But she did not listen. She ran home and soon forgot the poor frog.

The next day, the princess was sitting at dinner with the king. Suddenly, something came up the stone stairs, plitch, platch, plitch, platch. Then there was a knock on the door and a voice called, “Youngest princess, open the door for me!”
She opened the door and saw the frog. Quickly, she shut the door again and sat down. Her face was white.
“My child, why are you afraid?” asked the king. “Is there a giant at the door?”
“No, Father. It is a horrible frog.” And she told him everything about the ball and the promise.
The king looked serious. “You made a promise,” he said, “and you must keep it. Go and let him in.”

She opened the door, and the frog hopped in. He followed her to her chair. “Lift me up next to you,” he said. She did not want to, but the king told her to do it. Then the frog said, “Now push your little golden plate closer, so we can eat together.” The frog enjoyed his dinner very much, but the princess could not eat at all.
At last the frog said, “I have eaten enough, and I am tired. Carry me to your room and let me sleep in your bed.”
The princess began to cry. She did not want to touch the cold frog. But the king became angry. “He helped you when you needed help. You must not forget him now.”

So she picked up the frog with two fingers and carried him upstairs. She put him in a corner of her room. When she was in bed, the frog hopped over to her. “I am tired too,” he said. “Lift me up, or I will tell your father.”
Then the princess was very angry. She picked up the frog and threw him hard against the wall. “Now you can rest, you horrible frog!”
But when the frog fell to the floor, he was not a frog any more. He was a young prince with kind, beautiful eyes.
He told her his story. A wicked witch had put a spell on him, and only the princess could break it. The princess and the prince became good friends, and later, with the king’s blessing, they married.

The next morning, a carriage came to take them to the prince’s kingdom. At the back stood the prince’s loyal servant, Henry. When the prince became a frog, Henry was so sad that he put three iron bands around his heart, so it would not break. On the way, the prince heard a loud crack. “Henry, is the carriage breaking?” he asked.

“No, master,” said Henry. “It is the iron bands around my heart. My heart is so happy now that they are breaking.” Three times they heard the crack, and three times it was the iron around faithful Henry’s heart.
